evidence.interpretation: GMX's official docs (docs.gmx.io, HTTP 200) describe the DAO's four-phase proposal process. Phase 4 'Tally (Optional)' is the on-chain execution stage and lists six parameters: qualified-majority voting mechanism (65% + 1), quorum (view on Tally), 30,000-token proposal minimum, 24h voting delay, 5-day voting window, 24h execution delay. Five of those six parameters match the deployed GMX Governor on Arbitrum exactly: votingDelay()=86400 (24h), votingPeriod()=432000 (5 days), proposalThreshold()=30000e18 esGMX (30,000), and the governor's timelock 0x4bd1cdAab4254fC43ef6424653cA2375b4C94C0E (OZ TimelockController, listed as 'DAO Treasury' in GMX's own contract-addresses docs) has getMinDelay()=86400 (24h). The remaining parameter, the voting mechanism, does NOT match: COUNTING_MODE() at the pinned block returns 'support=bravo&quorum=bravo', the exact marker string of OpenZeppelin GovernorCountingSimple, under which proposal success is decided by simple majority (forVotes > againstVotes, i.e. 50%+1). No 65% threshold parameter exists anywhere in the governor's storage or logic; the contract is source-verified (Exact Match) on Arbiscan and implements the standard OZ counting module. The documented decision rule (65% qualified majority) therefore does not exist on chain: any proposal passing with 50-65% For votes succeeds on-chain contrary to the published rule.
evidence.docsSecondaryQuote: Phase 4: Tally (Optional): 'Voting mechanism: Qualified majority (65% + 1 of the smallest token unit) - Quorum: View current quorum on Tally - Minimum tokens to submit a proposal: 30,000 - Voting delay: 24 hours - Voting window: 5 days - Execution delay: 24 hours'
evidence.tvlNote: DefiLlama (api.llama.fi/protocol/gmx) reports GMX TVL around $210M at research time (2026-11-17), far above the $15M slot-4 floor for unindexed protocols.
evidence.additionalObservation: governor.quorum(block) returns 0 for all sampled blocks because the voting token's getPastTotalSupply returns 0 (esGMX carries no voting checkpoints). Flagged as an observation; the claim above rests on the documented 65% mechanism vs on-chain simple majority, which is deterministic at the pinned block.
evidence.docsCaveat: The docs page is GMX's current live governance documentation (fetched 2026-11-17, HTTP 200). Because five of the six published Phase-4 parameters reproduce the on-chain governor/timelock values exactly, the page is describing this exact deployment, and the voting-mechanism line is a live doc-vs-chain divergence, not stale text about a retired contract.
